title: You think you’re losing…
paragraphs:
You think you’re losing…
but what if God told you to stop fighting?

You came ready to attack.
God told you to walk.

You wanted progress.
God gave you repetition.

You expected breakthrough.
God gave you silence.
And now you’re asking the question nobody says out loud:
“Did I miss God… or is this just not working?”
Let me pull you into Jericho.

Dust in the air.
Walls towering like they’re mocking you.
Enemies watching from above.

Day 1… nothing.
Day 2… still nothing.
Day 3… people are starting to whisper.

Day 4… doubt gets louder.
Day 5… your faith starts negotiating.
Day 6… embarrassment sets in.
Because obedience that doesn’t produce visible results feels like failure.
Some of you are there right now.

You’ve been praying… but the addiction is still there.
You’ve been obeying… but the door is still closed.
You’ve been faithful… but the breakthrough hasn’t come.
And deep inside, a quiet voice whispers:
But here’s the truth Jericho reveals:
God is doing His deepest work when it looks like nothing is happening.
“By faith the walls of Jericho fell, after they had been encircled for seven days.” — Hebrews 11:30
“The LORD said to Joshua, ‘See, I have given Jericho into your hand…’” — Joshua 6:2

Before the march.
Before the shout.
Before the walls moved.
God declared victory before evidence existed.

Some scholars interpret this as a divine pattern:
God settles things in the spiritual realm before they manifest in the physical.

Your silence season is not empty.
It’s loaded.

It was pride.
It was fear.
It was the illusion that strength wins battles.
And God was dismantling something deeper than walls.
Because if Israel fought and won, they would trust their swords.
But if they walked and won—
And this is where it hits you.
Because your “Jericho” isn’t just your problem.

The need to fix yourself.
The urge to control outcomes.
The silent belief that if you try harder, you’ll finally break through.
But God interrupts that narrative and says:
Not because the battle isn’t real.
But because you are not the savior in this story.
Some of you aren’t just tired.

Ashamed that you’re still struggling.
Ashamed that you’re still circling the same issue.
Ashamed that after all your prayers… you’re still here.

Same temptation.
Same weakness.
Same quiet battle no one sees.
📖 “There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.” — Romans 8:1

Not less condemnation.
Not delayed condemnation.
Which means your Jericho isn’t proof that God abandoned you.
It’s proof that God is working on you.
✝️ GOSPEL TURN — THIS IS WHERE EVERYTHING CHANGES
Because Jericho is not the main story.
But your greatest wall is sin.

A barrier you cannot climb.
A separation you cannot fix.
📖 “For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” — Romans 3:23
And no amount of walking… striving… or self-improvement can tear it down.
He didn’t ask you to circle your sin.
He sent His Son to crush it.

Jesus lived the life you couldn’t live.
Perfect. Sinless. Obedient.
Then He went to the cross—
📖 “He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree…” — 1 Peter 2:24

Every failure.
Every secret.
Every shame you hide.
The wall between you and God?
📖 “If the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed.” — John 8:36
So what do you do now?
But because victory has already been declared in Christ.
Because faith is not proven in outcomes.
You are not circling in vain.
Every step of obedience is stacking pressure in the unseen.
Every moment of surrender is weakening something you can’t yet see.

Not your performance.
Not your perfection.
Or maybe you’re tired of walking altogether.
Jesus is not waiting for you to get it right.
He’s inviting you to come home.
📖 “Come to me, all who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.” — Matthew 11:28
Because the greatest miracle isn’t walls falling.
